findings.statement: Application permissions (letting an app run with no signed-in user) can only be consented to by a Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator; an application granted a broad permission like Files.Read.All can read any file in the organization.
findings.excerpt: can read any file in the organization

findings.statement: Only a Global Administrator can grant org-wide admin consent to a Teams app's requested Graph permissions; Teams Administrators can view the required permissions but can't grant the consent themselves.
findings.sourceTitle: Grant and manage consent to Teams app permissions

findings.statement: Publisher verification requires a completed Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (CPP) account and an Entra user with Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator rights; once verified, a badge appears on the app's consent screen.
findings.sourceTitle: Mark an app as publisher verified

findings.statement: Listing an app on the Teams Store means it's thoroughly reviewed against the Microsoft Commercial Marketplace certification policies, with a focus on deep functional and user-experience testing, usability checks, and metadata checks, across desktop, web, and mobile clients.
Microsoft aims to provide a detailed test report within 24 working hours of submission.
Once all required issues are resolved, allow at least one business day for the app to become available in the Teams Store.

A Microsoft blog post recommended planning 1 to 1.5 months between submission and a desired publish date, since most of that time goes to developers fixing issues found across multiple rounds of validation.
findings.sourceTitle: Publish your apps to the Microsoft Teams store

findings.statement: Validation issues are categorized as Must fix (required before approval), Blocker (prevents further testing until resolved), or Good-to-fix (optional improvements); fixes are resubmitted for revalidation until every required issue is resolved.
Before submitting, create a Partner Center developer account, complete publisher verification, and validate your app package in the Teams Developer Portal to catch errors early.
Microsoft Teams integrations in Composio use Microsoft Graph OAuth scopes rather than Teams resource-specific consent (RSC) permissions in the OAuth authorize URL.

Delegated permissions let an app act for a signed-in user and, depending on the permission, can sometimes be consented to by the user themselves rather than an admin; Microsoft recommends using delegated permissions wherever they meet the app's needs.
findings.excerpt: delegated permission model is the recommended approach

claim.text: Registering an app and requesting Graph permissions is self-serve; publisher verification needs a Cloud Partner Program account but is optional, not required to use the app.
Listing an app on the Teams Store means it's thoroughly reviewed against the Microsoft Commercial Marketplace certification policies before it can appear there.
Only a Global Administrator can consent to application permissions (and to org-wide admin consent for a Teams app's Graph permissions generally).

tierReason.text: Listing an app on the Teams Store triggers deep functional, user-experience, and metadata review against Microsoft's Commercial Marketplace certification policies, with revalidation rounds until every required issue is resolved.

claim.text: Microsoft aims to deliver an initial test report within 24 working hours, but a full submission-to-publish cycle has been estimated at 1 to 1.5 months once revalidation rounds are included.

scopeForks.text: A custom (unlisted) Teams app that a customer's admin uploads or sideloads directly doesn't need to pass Teams Store review at all - that review is required only for Teams Store/AppSource listing. The customer-admin consent gate (for admin-level Graph permissions) applies either way, listed or not.

claim.text: It's unclear whether Composio offers Microsoft Teams as a fully managed toolkit; its Teams guide instead focuses on using Microsoft Graph OAuth scopes correctly instead of Teams resource-specific consent permissions.

whatYouLose.text: On a managed app, the consent screen shows the platform's name and brand instead of yours, and scopes and rate limits are typically fixed rather than something you control.

whenToSwitch.text: Switch to your own Entra app registration once you need your own branding, specific Graph permissions, or your own rate limits.

flow.text: A developer registers an app in Microsoft Entra, requests delegated and/or application Graph permissions, and users (or a Global Administrator, for admin-only permissions) grant consent before the app can access their data.

appTypes.text: Delegated permissions act on behalf of a signed-in user; application permissions let the app run with no signed-in user and can be far broader, such as reading every file in the organization.

tokenNotes.text: Publisher verification associates an app with a verified Cloud Partner Program account, surfacing a verified badge to users on the consent screen.

scopes.allows: Lets the app run with no signed-in user, with access as broad as reading every file in the organization.
scopes.neededFor: Background services or automations that act without a specific user present.

claim.text: Only a Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator can consent to application permissions, which can be very broad.

scopes.allows: Lets the app act on behalf of a signed-in user, scoped to what that user can access.
scopes.neededFor: Most integrations that act on a specific user's behalf rather than running in the background.

claim.text: Microsoft recommends delegated permissions wherever they meet the app's needs, since some can be user-consentable rather than admin-only.
Publishing to the Teams Store requires a Partner Center developer account.

prerequisites.item: Completed publisher verification (recommended before submitting, via a Cloud Partner Program account)

claim.text: Microsoft recommends completing publisher verification before you submit your app for the Teams Store.

prerequisites.item: A validated app package (checked in the Teams Developer Portal) plus test notes

claim.text: Validating your app package in the Teams Developer Portal catches errors before submission.

steps.title: Found Microsoft's Graph permissions, publisher verification, and Teams Store docs
steps.detail: The research stage located Microsoft's official documentation across Entra, Graph, and Teams Store publishing.

claims.text: Microsoft documents Graph permissions, publisher verification, and Teams Store publishing at learn.microsoft.com.

steps.title: Register your app in Microsoft Entra and request Graph permissions
steps.detail: Choose delegated permissions where possible; application permissions need a Global Administrator to consent.

claims.text: Delegated permissions are recommended wherever they meet the app's needs.

steps.title: Build your consent and (if needed) admin-consent flow
steps.detail: Application permissions, and org-wide Teams app consent generally, can only be granted by a Global Administrator.

claims.text: Only a Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator can consent to application permissions.

steps.title: Complete publisher verification
steps.detail: Needs a completed Cloud Partner Program account; adds a verified badge to your app's consent screen.

claims.text: Publisher verification requires a completed Cloud Partner Program account.

steps.title: Live for any customer who installs or sideloads the app - no Teams Store review needed
steps.detail: A custom app a customer's admin uploads directly doesn't need Teams Store review.

steps.title: Draft your scope justification
steps.detail: Use the Scope justification helper to prepare reviewer-facing notes for each Graph permission you request.

steps.title: Draft a customer admin note
steps.detail: Use the Customer admin note helper, since a Global Administrator must grant org-wide consent.

steps.title: Create a Partner Center developer account and validate your app package
steps.detail: Required before submitting to the Teams Store; validate in the Teams Developer Portal first to catch errors.

claims.text: A Partner Center developer account and a validated app package are both needed before submission.

steps.title: Submit to the Teams Store and resolve validation feedback
steps.detail: Expect an initial test report within about 24 working hours, then possibly several rounds of revalidation.

claims.text: Microsoft provides a detailed test report within 24 working hours and categorizes issues as Must fix, Blocker, or Good-to-fix.

steps.title: Approved and published to the Teams Store
steps.detail: Once there are no remaining required issues, allow at least one business day to appear in the store.

claims.text: Allow at least one business day for the app to become available in the Teams Store once approved.

provider.who: Microsoft's Teams Store validation team (concierge service)
provider.what: Reviews listed apps against Commercial Marketplace certification policies with deep functional, UX, and metadata checks; not required for a custom app a customer uploads directly.

claims.text: Teams Store listing is reviewed against Commercial Marketplace certification policies across desktop, web, and mobile.

customerAdmin.who: A Global Administrator at the customer's organization
customerAdmin.what: Must grant org-wide admin consent for any admin-only (application) Graph permission the app requests; Teams Administrators can view but not grant this.

claims.text: Only a Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator can consent to application permissions.

endUser.what: Consents individually for delegated permissions the organization's policy allows users to grant themselves.

claims.text: Delegated permissions can sometimes be consented to by the user themselves rather than an admin.

stuckPoints.reason: Validation flags a 'Blocker' issue, stopping further testing
stuckPoints.fix: Resolve Blocker issues first - the validation team can't test the rest of the app's functionality until they're fixed.

claim.text: Blocker issues prevent the validation team from testing further until they're resolved.

stuckPoints.reason: Submission-to-publish timeline runs much longer than expected
stuckPoints.fix: Budget 1 to 1.5 months for a full cycle, since most of the time goes to fixing issues across multiple validation rounds.

claim.text: A full submission-to-publish cycle has been estimated at 1 to 1.5 months, mostly spent fixing validation issues.

whileYouWait.text: A custom app can be uploaded or sideloaded directly by a customer's admin and used immediately, without ever going through Teams Store review.
